claims.text: Adding 3–5 wt% graphene nanosheets to the HEA during powder-metallurgy processing can form a well-dispersed conductive network in the alloy matrix.
Graphene nanosheets will bridge HEA grains and improve intergranular connectivity.
The graphene network will create continuous channels for rapid heat transport through the HEA.
Dispersed graphene nanosheets will reinforce the HEA microstructure.
Graphene has sufficiently high intrinsic thermal conductivity to provide additional electron- and phonon-transport pathways in the HEA.
Uniformly distributed graphene nanosheets will limit grain-boundary sliding.
Uniformly distributed graphene nanosheets will limit microcracking.
Limiting grain-boundary sliding and microcracking will preserve the mechanical strength of the graphene-modified HEA.
The graphene-modified HEA will retain its proposed benefits at approximately 700–1000°C under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading representative of plasma-facing reactor service.
Adding 3–5 wt% graphene will increase thermal conductivity by approximately 10–20% relative to an otherwise comparable unmodified HEA.
Adding 3–5 wt% graphene will cause less than 10% degradation in yield strength and other key mechanical properties relative to the unmodified HEA.
The simultaneous thermal and mechanical benefits will occur only when graphene content remains within the 3–5 wt% range.
Excessive graphene addition or poor graphene dispersion could reduce both thermal and mechanical performance.
Dispersion quality and graphene–HEA interfacial bonding may affect scalability and reproducibility.
